comments.body:
## Review and fix of Lemma (Adjoint representation), the main rigor gap

The issue was the generic proof-task placeholder, so I audited the full solution for genuine mathematical gaps. The substantive content of parts (a)-(c) is sound (I numerically reverified the commutant dimension counts in Lemma 1.2(iv), the eigenvalue-multiplicity correspondence between Lambda(Q), chi(Q), and chi(Q)_R, and the LQR/Newton/GD reductions). The one place that was **not rigorous** was the proof of the central Lemma "Adjoint representation" (lem:chi), which asserted

  Q >= 0  <=>  Lambda(Q) >= 0  <=>  chi(Q) >= 0

and the eigenvalue-multiplicity statement via the hand-wave "the complex form w*chi(Q)w has real part xhat^T Lambda(Q) xhat up to the fixed factor coming from C=R^2; concretely Lambda(Q) is similar to the real form of chi(Q)." No isomorphism was exhibited and the doubling/quadrupling of multiplicities was not actually proved. Since prop:hermconvex, thm:uniqueness, and thm:pmp all depend on this equivalence, this was a real gap.

### Fix
Replaced the proof with a constructive one built on an explicit R-linear **intertwiner**

  Theta : H^n -> C^{2n},  x_r = z_r + w_r j  |->  (..., z_r, -conj(w_r), ...),

proving rigorously:
- (a) Theta is an R-linear bijection;
- (b) Theta(Ax) = chi(A) Theta(x)  (from the scalar identity qx = (z1 z - z2 conj(w)) + (z1 w + z2 conj(z)) j);
- (c) Theta is an isometry:  <x,y> = Re(Theta(x)* Theta(y)).

From (b),(c) and Hermiticity of chi(Q):  Real(x^H Q x) = Theta(x)* chi(Q) Theta(x) = xhat^T Lambda(Q) xhat, and since both xhat and Theta(x) range over the whole spaces, the three positivity notions coincide (strict versions too).

For multiplicities I made the similarity explicit: with the real embedding e:C^{2n}->R^{4n}, the matrix U = (e o Theta) o (hat)^{-1} is **orthogonal**, and polarization of xhat^T Lambda(Q) xhat = (U xhat)^T chi(Q)_R (U xhat) on symmetric matrices gives the exact identity Lambda(Q) = U^T chi(Q)_R U. Hence Lambda(Q) and chi(Q)_R are orthogonally similar; with the doubling chi(Q) -> chi(Q)_R this yields multiplicity 2m (and 4 for chi-simple eigenvalues). Even-multiplicity of chi(Q) is proved via the conjugate-linear J with J^2 = -I commuting with chi(Q).

### Numerical verification (all passed)
- commutant dim {R_i,R_j,R_k} = {L_i,L_j,L_k} = 4;
- spectrum(Lambda(Q)) = spectrum(chi(Q)) doubled, for many random Hermitian Q;
- the intertwiner identities Theta(qx)=chi(q)Theta(x) and <x,y>=Re(Theta(x)* Theta(y));
- the exact orthogonal similarity Lambda(Q) = U^T chi(Q)_R U with U orthogonal.

Also fixed a sign typo in the displayed expansion of the second component of Theta(qx) and replaced psmallmatrix with amsmath-compatible smallmatrix. No LaTeX toolchain is installed in the workspace; brace/environment/$-delimiter balances were checked manually.

The lemma -- and hence the optimization theory depending on it -- is now rigorously established. Resolving.
